newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Mogas down, naphtha up on crude.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Mogas down, naphtha up on crude.

text.p: Gasoline prices slipped on a lack of demand while naphtha firmed slightly with crude, traders said on Tuesday.
The same European major emerged to sell 50,000 barrels of 92-octane supplies at $22.50 for July 8-12 loading.
The major said he needed to sell off some stocks as fundamentals were weak.
The lack of bids were evident that the market is soft, he said.
Naptha market has drifted into a quiet period with most North Asian traders away at the open-specification contract meeting being held in Japan.
Talks today centred on South Korean firms withdrawing their proposals to convert their status in open-spec naphtha trading from buyer to seller, participants told Reuters in Tokyo.
The two-day meeting was expected to end on Tuesday.
Traders said prices tracked crude to end higher. August Brent on London's IPE was last traded at $18.08, up 10 cents from Monday.

Enquiries from earlier anticipated demand from Thailand dissappeard as sources said a downturn in petrochemical demand and the switch of feedstock from naphtha to liquified petroluem gas dampened buying interests.
Taiwan's tender to buy 28,000 tonnes of August napthenic and aromatic naphtha for August 1-31 delivery closed on Wedeneday and would be valid for two days.
